entries.head: put on

senses.en: to dress yourself in something

example.en: Put on a jacket — the office AC is freezing.
example.zh: 穿件外套，办公室空调太冷了。

entries.l1_note: “穿”有两个词：put on 是穿上的动作，wear 是穿着的状态。中文一个“穿”。

entries.head: try on

senses.en: to put clothes on to see if they fit

example.en: Can I try this on? The fitting room is over there, right?
example.zh: 这件我可以试一下吗？试衣间在那边对吧？

entries.l1_note: 试穿是 try on，不是 try it（少了 on）；代词夹中间：try it on。

entries.head: dress up

senses.en: to wear formal or nicer clothes than usual

example.en: Do we need to dress up for the dinner, or is jeans fine?
example.zh: 晚饭要穿正式点吗，还是牛仔裤就行？

entries.l1_note: “打扮”不是 make up（那是化妆）；穿得好是 dress up。

entries.head: dress down

senses.en: to wear more casual clothes than usual

example.en: The company lets us dress down on Fridays.
example.zh: 公司周五允许穿便装。

entries.l1_note: dress down 还有“责备”的意思，看上下文。

entries.head: throw on

senses.en: to put clothes on quickly without much thought

example.en: I threw on a hoodie and ran downstairs for the delivery.
example.zh: 我随手套了件卫衣就下楼拿外卖。

entries.l1_note: “随手穿”不是 wear casually 才自然；throw on 有“随便一抓”的画面。

entries.head: slip on

senses.en: to put on shoes or clothes quickly and easily

example.en: Slip on your sneakers — we're leaving in two minutes.
example.zh: 把运动鞋蹬上，两分钟后走。

entries.l1_note: slip on 暗示不用系带、一蹬就进；系带的鞋用 put on。

entries.head: zip up

senses.en: to close a piece of clothing with a zipper

example.en: Zip up — it's freezing outside and you're wearing it open.
example.zh: 拉上拉链，外面冻死了，你还敞着穿。

entries.l1_note: “闭嘴”是 zip it，不是 zip up；zip up 只指拉链。

entries.head: button up

senses.en: to fasten the buttons on a shirt or coat

example.en: Button up your shirt before the interview starts.
example.zh: 面试开始前把衬衫扣好。

entries.l1_note: 扣扣子是 button up，不是 close the buttons（中式）。

entries.head: lace up

senses.en: to tie the laces of your shoes

example.en: Lace up properly — the trail is slippery.
example.zh: 鞋带系好，山路很滑。

entries.l1_note: 系鞋带是 lace up / tie your shoes，不说 fasten the shoes。

entries.head: roll up

senses.en: to fold the bottom of sleeves or pants upward

example.en: Roll up your sleeves — the sink is clogged again.
example.zh: 把袖子卷起来，水槽又堵了。

entries.l1_note: roll up 也指“到场、陆续抵达”，比如 roll up to the party。

entries.head: tuck in

senses.en: to push the bottom of a shirt into your pants

example.en: Tuck in your shirt — you look like you just got out of bed.
example.zh: 把衬衫塞进去，你这样像刚起床。

entries.l1_note: 英式里 tuck in 还可以是“开吃”，美式少用；这里只讲穿衣。

entries.head: go with

senses.en: to look good together with something else

example.en: Do these shoes go with the dress, or is it too much?
example.zh: 这双鞋配这条裙子吗，会不会太夸张？

entries.l1_note: “配”不是 match with 才常用；口语说 go with。

entries.head: match up

senses.en: when two things look the same or fit together

example.en: The bag doesn't match up with the rest of the outfit.
example.zh: 这个包和整套搭配对不上。

entries.l1_note: match up 强调“对得上”，go with 强调“配着好看”。

entries.head: stand out

senses.en: to be easy to notice because of how you look

example.en: Wear something bright if you want to stand out in the photos.
example.zh: 想拍照显眼就穿亮色。

entries.l1_note: “显眼”不是 be obvious；stand out 是褒义居多。

entries.head: cover up

senses.zh: 用衣服遮住不想露的地方
senses.en: to put something over part of your body

example.en: Bring a cardigan to cover up if the restaurant is cold.
example.zh: 餐厅冷的话带件开衫遮一下。

entries.l1_note: cover up 还有“掩盖（错误）”的意思，穿衣语境看宾语。

entries.head: strip off

senses.en: to take off your clothes quickly

example.en: We stripped off our wet jackets the moment we got inside.
example.zh: 一进门我们就把湿外套脱了。

entries.l1_note: strip off 比较口语、常指整套；单件脱用 take off。

entries.head: change into

senses.en: to take off what you are wearing and put on something else

example.en: I need ten minutes to change into something nicer.
example.zh: 给我十分钟换身好点的。

entries.l1_note: “换衣服”不是 change clothes 才完整；换成某套用 change into。

entries.head: change out of

senses.en: to take off the clothes you are wearing

example.en: Change out of your work clothes before dinner.
example.zh: 晚饭前把工作服换下来。

entries.l1_note: into 是换成什么，out of 是脱掉什么；方向别反。

entries.head: break in

senses.en: to make new shoes comfortable by wearing them

example.en: These boots need a week to break in — my heels are destroyed.
example.zh: 这双靴子得穿一周才服帖，我脚后跟已经废了。

entries.l1_note: break in 还有“闯入”，鞋的语境才指“穿服帖”。

entries.head: take in

senses.en: to make a piece of clothing smaller by sewing

example.en: I had the waist taken in — it fits perfectly now.
example.zh: 我让裁缝把腰收了一下，现在正合身。

entries.l1_note: 改小是 take in，放宽是 let out；take in 还有“吸收、理解”。

entries.head: let out

senses.en: to make a piece of clothing wider by sewing

example.en: Can the tailor let out these pants a little?
example.zh: 裁缝能把这条裤子放宽一点吗？

entries.l1_note: let out 也指“放学、下课”和“发出声音”，看语境。

entries.head: pick out

senses.en: to choose something from a group

example.en: She picked out a coat for me in five minutes.
example.zh: 她五分钟就给我挑好了一件外套。

entries.l1_note: 挑衣服用 pick out；pick up 是拿起或接人。

entries.head: fit into

senses.en: to be the right size for your body

example.en: I still can't fit into my old jeans after the holidays.
example.zh: 过完节我还是穿不进那条旧牛仔裤。

entries.l1_note: “穿得下”不是 can wear it（也对但弱）；fit into 强调尺码。

entries.head: wear out

senses.en: to use clothes until they are damaged

example.en: I wore out two pairs of sneakers this year.
example.zh: 我今年穿坏了两双球鞋。

entries.l1_note: wear out 也指“累垮”，人做宾语时是精疲力尽。

entries.head: layer up

senses.en: to wear several layers of clothes

example.en: Layer up — the temperature drops ten degrees after dark.
example.zh: 多叠几层，天黑后要降十度。

entries.l1_note: “多穿几层”现在是穿搭常用词，不是 fancy 说法。

entries.head: show off

senses.en: to try to make people notice something you have

example.en: He wore the new watch to the party just to show it off.
example.zh: 他戴着新表去聚会，就是为了显摆。

entries.l1_note: “炫”不是 show people（太泛）；show off 才是显摆。
collocations: show off in front of friends

entries.head: set off

senses.en: to make something look better by contrast

example.en: The black dress sets off the gold earrings really well.
example.zh: 黑裙子把金耳环衬得特别好看。

entries.l1_note: set off 也指“出发”（set off for the airport），颜色语境才是衬托。

entries.head: pull off

senses.zh: 大胆的穿法也能穿好看
senses.en: to succeed in wearing something bold or difficult

example.en: Not everyone can pull off neon green, but she does.
example.zh: 荧光绿不是谁都能驾驭，她就行。

entries.l1_note: pull off 原义是“成功办成难事”，穿搭里指“穿得住”。

entries.head: suit up

senses.en: to put on a formal suit

example.en: Suit up — the client meeting moved up to nine.
example.zh: 穿正装，客户会提前到九点了。

entries.l1_note: suit up 偏口语、带点玩笑感；正式写作不用。

entries.head: show through

senses.zh: 里面的东西透过外衣看得见
senses.en: when what is underneath can be seen through the fabric

example.en: The white dress is cute, but everything shows through in sunlight.
example.zh: 白裙子好看是好看，太阳底下什么都透。

entries.l1_note: “透”不是 see inside；衣物透视用 show through。
